# ADR 0034 §2.3 item 2: a denied external link is handed to the system browser

## Context

neomjs/neo-agent-institution#493 (FM v1): in the packaged Fleet Manager an external link does nothing. The catch-up view renders PR citations as `<a target="_blank">`, and the merge-queue rows of neomjs/neo-agent-institution#449 want to link their PRs; the shell's `setWindowOpenHandler` returns `{action: 'deny'}` for every URL `isHarnessPopupUrl` refuses, and nothing in the harness calls `shell.openExternal`. That is exactly the fail-closed window policy ADR 0034 §2.3 item 2 specifies — ALLOW same-origin harness URLs, DENY everything else — and the ADR names no hand-off to the system browser. The implementation leaf's own order: amend the ADR first, then the harness.

## The Problem

The policy's intent is that no foreign document ever renders inside the shell, and that intent is right. Its letter also forbids the one thing a cockpit must do with a pull-request URL: open it where the operator reads GitHub. Without the amendment the Institution leaf would be implementation-before-authority (the #17919 class).

## The Architectural Reality

- ADR 0034 §2.3 item 2 (`learn/agentos/decisions/0034-electron-shell-architecture.md`), already amended once in place for the `about:blank` staging realm (#19237, 2026-09-26) — the precedent for the shape of this amendment: an in-place paragraph with a provenance bracket, naming the admitted thing and its bounds.
- Electron: `setWindowOpenHandler` runs for `window.open()` and for `target="_blank"` anchors; `{action: 'deny'}` cancels the window; `shell.openExternal(url)` opens the URL in the OS default browser.
- The consumer side: `harness/contentPolicy.mjs` (`isHarnessPopupUrl`), `harness/main.mjs` (`configureWebContents`), neomjs/neo-agent-institution#493.

## The Fix

One paragraph appended to §2.3 item 2, in the #19237 shape: **The external hand-off** *(amended 2026-10-03, this ticket — for neomjs/neo-agent-institution#493)*: a denied window-open whose URL is `https:` on an allowlisted host (`github.com`; additions amend this paragraph) and carries no credentials is handed to the system browser with `shell.openExternal`; the in-app window stays denied, `will-navigate` is unchanged (same-window off-origin navigation stays denied), and nothing foreign renders in the shell. The §5 E3 row gains the hand-off in its scope cell. No other statement moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §2.3 item 2 carries the external hand-off paragraph with its provenance bracket, the `https:` + allowlisted-host + no-credentials bound, the unchanged `will-navigate`, and the named consumer.
- [ ] The §5 E3 row names the external hand-off beside the allowlist.
- [ ] No other ADR statement changes (diff limited to those two sites).

## Out of Scope

The harness implementation (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#493); any host beyond `github.com`; browsing external pages inside the app.

## Related

neomjs/neo-agent-institution#493 (the consumer leaf; depends on this). #19237 (the amendment precedent). neomjs/neo-agent-institution#7 (the shell epic).
